text:
lina: quick note - ptq onboarding for 'harbor-lite' shows uptick in funcall parse failures for streaming multi-turns (6-9% vs 0.7% fp16).

canary-bot: Canary alert: funcall_parse_failure_rate = 7.8% for harbor-lite-ptq (5m). dashboard: https://canary.internal/harbor-lite/ptq

pat: can anyone paste one raw concatenated example? even one truncated chunk helps with triage.

jorge: here's a cleaned concat of streaming chunks from a failed session:
{"action":"ack","args":{"task":77,"status":"started"}

{"action":"complete","args":{"task":77,"result":"ok"}}

note the missing close and then a new object.

evelyn: sounds like last-token cutoff. harbor-lite used int8 PTQ and streaming + kvcache reuse. check whether eos/token merging changed after quant.

lina: short triage plan: (1) run 1k-session grid: streaming on/off x kvcache on/off x batch 1/3, (2) collect last 6 token ids for failed sessions to S3 (secure), (3) implement a conservative repair that only accepts repairs preserving top-level action string.

pat: also add metric: repaired_changed_action_count and repair_confidence (0-1). block automatic repair for high-risk actions.

jorge: temporary mitigation: opt-out streaming for ptq canary traffic until we know whether token-id shift is the root cause.

lina: assigning: @pat -> add metrics & conservative repair; @jorge -> token-id dumps + grid; @evelyn -> run non-stream mirror baseline.

pat: starting work now, will push small parser-rescue lib behind a feature flag.

lina: tl;dr: ptq streaming shows parse regressions. short-term: conservative repairs + telemetry + possible streaming pause. medium-term: tokenizer bisect for quant-induced token id drift.
